calls.reason: The Paleka paper shows forecasting is hard to evaluate, and Halawi's self-supervised method uses resolved questions. Neither shows synthetic data working or failing for novel geopolitical or economic counterfactuals, so the evidence is thin and adjacent.

The 2016 'Playing for Data' paper confirms roughly nine years of synthetic training data. Waymo's May 2025 post shows driverless service in only four cities, which is bounded deployment, not general autonomy.
The only study measures legislator engagement with AI policy narratives. Nothing isolates whether AGI-imminence narratives accelerated competitive AI development.
The packet has only the AI 2027 authors' stated aims and a June 2025 House letter with competitive rhetoric. No decision record or causal study ties the narratives to faster development.
ITU ownership figures and the St. Louis Fed generative-AI adoption survey measure reach for different populations. None compares accumulated economic or social impact across the three technologies.
